Order 
With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 08.08.2023 passed in MACC No.55/2022 by the 1st Addl.
Member
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, District Dhar, whereby a total sum of Rs.12,68,245/- has been awarded to the appellants by way of compensation

. 
3. Facts of the case are that on on 22.12.2021 at about 5.00 deceased Lalsingh with his wife was going on his motorcycle bearing registration No.M.P. 11 MS 8846 from Ranikhedi to Rajgarh.

The offending car bearing registration No.G.J. 14 BA 6003 came rashly and negligently, driven and owned by respondent No.1 dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased as NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9015 2 MA-7202-2023 a result of which the deceased died on the spot.

The FIR was registered at crime No.348/2021 under Section 279, 337, 304A and 338 of IPC.
4.
Thereafter appellant filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.2 by filing its written statement to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellants as aforesaid.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the learned tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at the rate of Rs.7325/- per month, which as per the Minimum Wages Act should be Rs.8,800/- prevailing on the date of accident.
Hence it is submitted that the income of the deceased be assessed at the rate of Rs.8,800/- per month.

He further submits that on the head of future Smt. Sitabai vs Sandeep on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102202174/
1 prospects and rise in income the tribunal has given only 10% whereas looking to the age of the deceased at the time of accident to be 42 years as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680 (para 59.3 & 59.4) it should be 25%.

sentences.text: On these grounds, it is prayed that appropriate income be enhanced and appeal be allowed.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the prayer with further submission that appropriate amount has been awarded in the head of future prospects and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:9015 3 MA-7202-2023 for the parties and perused the record.
8.

It is not in dispute that income if not proved by cogent evidence, it should be taken as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh on the date of accident i.e. on 22.12.2021 income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.8800/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour', whereas the learned Claims Tribunal has taken the income as Rs.7325/- only.

9. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
For loss of 13,86,000 (Rs.8800/- per month + 25% F.P. - 1/4th Dependency x 12 x 14 = Rs.13,86,000/- Filial Rs.2,20,000/-
consortium Funeral Rs.16,500/-
expenses For loss of Rs.16,500/-
 Estate  Total Rs.16,39,000/-
 MACT Award Rs.12,68,000/-
 Enhanced  Rs.3,71,000/-
 Amount 10.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.3,71,000/-(Rs.16,39,000 - Rs.12,68,000) as against the award of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9015 4 MA-7202-2023 Tribunal of Rs.12,68,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.3,71,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
